text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: packet-loss spike detected for outbound traffic to eu-west-2 (multiple prefixes) via TransitWave / CarrierX. Severity: high. Pager: oncall-net.

oncall-net: paging in. seeing ~25-40% packet loss on egress to a handful of customer-facing prefixes in eu-west-2. impact: 5% of requests failing, intermittent 502s.

morgan: digging in, can you paste the traceroute + pings? also which POP / AZ is showing it (sfo vs ord vs lhr)?

oncall-net: LHR and AMS POPs primarily. quick pings from lhr-egress-03: 
```
$ ping -c 10 203.0.113.45
--- 203.0.113.45 ping statistics ---
10 packets transmitted, 6 received, 40% packet loss, time 9003ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 10.2/15.4/45.6/8.1 ms
```

morgan: traceroute shows churn at TransitWave's ASN edge:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  *  *  *
 4  203.0.113.1  12.3 ms  12.1 ms  12.2 ms
 5  203.0.113.45  13.5 ms  14.1 ms  13.9 ms
```
(we see several hops time out intermittently between our egress and TransitWave edge)

tara: any BGP flaps? run a quick bgp summary from lhr-egress-03 pls.

oncall-net: pulling BGP adjshows now, truncated: 
```
BGP adjacency summary (filtered):
Neighbor        AS      State/PfxRcd  Uptime
10.11.12.1      64512   Established   00:02:14
203.0.113.254  54113   Active        00:00:30  <-- flapping
203.0.113.253  64567   Established   12:34:56
```

eng-sre: 203.0.113.254 is TransitWave edge. "Active" indicates the session is not stable. I'm seeing repeated BGP NOTIFICATION messages from that neighbor in the control-plane logs.

morgan: tagging carrierops and eng-sre. @carrierops can you confirm whether TransitWave is experiencing an upstream flap? we need a parallel channel to ask for mitigation (community resets, dampening adjustments, or temporary prepends).

carrierops: joining. we see TransitWave reporting high route churn on their peering fabric to AS54113. internal telemetry shows packet drops and queueing at their metro aggregation. they are acknowledging a regional maintenance + an unexpected failure on a linecard. working on a failover. estimated time to stable: 15-30m.

product-ops: customer impact check: which customers/routes are affected? any paid customers in EU experiencing full outages?

oncall-net: preliminary metrics: ~2.3% of total API traffic impacted, but for three EU customers traffic loss is >50% for a 5-10 minute window. errors are mostly 502/504 and a subset of long tail timeouts.

eng-sre: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic away from TransitWave where alternate peers exist (we have backup sessions via CarrierX-AS64567 and EdgeNV-AS3356) 2) announce prefix with shorter prepended path to prefer backup peers 3) enable temporary emergency BGP community to encourage de-preference on TransitWave (only if carrier confirms acceptance) 4) monitor errors and revert when stable.

morgan: start plan: enable traffic steering on lhr-pop to prefer CarrierX/EdgeNV for the affected prefixes. I'll run the announce change in 60s unless any objections.

oncall-net: go for it. posting the specific commands we use: 
```
# announce with local-pref tweak (example)
configure bgp neighbor 203.0.113.253 route-map OUT-to-CarrierX
route-map OUT-to-CarrierX permit 10
 set local-preference 200
commit
```

morgan: executed local-pref change on lhr and ams POPs. monitoring BGP table and egress flows.

carrierops: TransitWave reports they've initiated the on-site linecard replacement and are steering traffic across remaining capacity. they see reduced packet loss but BGP session still oscillates sporadically.

oncall-net: after local-pref change, packet loss to 203.0.113.45 improved from 40% -> 2% from lhr-egress-03. analytics show 503 error rate for EU decreased by ~75% in the last 5m.

eng-sre: confirm: we've not blackholed or withdrawn prefixes, just adjusted preference. please keep an eye on path diversity for the next 2 hours. we'll keep canary traffic on TransitWave for monitoring.

morgan: initiated synthetic canaries to the affected customer endpoints, running 1req/s to each to track regressions.

product-ops: flagged impacted accounts and opened support cases, sending temporary status note to customers. we should prepare a short post-incident summary once stable.

tara: handoff incoming: my shift ends in 18m, @morgan you take oncall for next 2 hours? once TransitWave confirms stable for 30m escalate closure.

morgan: ack, taking handoff. will keep channel updated every 10m.

carrierops: TransitWave confirms green on packet-loss graphs and linecard replaced. BGP session flaps have stopped for the last 3m. they will monitor for another 30m before fully closing the ticket.

oncall-net: observed BGP state -> Established for 203.0.113.254, no NOTIFICATION in logs.

eng-sre: metrics look back to baseline. canary requests all passing. error budget impact estimated: 0.02% of monthly requests. recommend we de-escalate but keep watch.

incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated. Duration: ~23 minutes from initial alert to mitigation. Incident commander: morgan. Follow-up: create postmortem and include TransitWave RCA and our pre-approved traffic steering playbook.

morgan: filing follow-up ticket ENGNET-4872 for postmortem + action items (review peering SLAs with TransitWave, automate local-pref steering for specific prefixes, improve alerting thresholds to reduce MTTA). assigning to eng-sre and carrierops.

product-ops: sending customer-facing update now. thanks all. :tada:
